nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Target expression: べきだ. Intended meaning: A duty or norm, rather than personal advice. Compared alternatives: ことだ. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 请选最符合提示意思和语气的一项。其他选项换个语境也可能成立，但这里要的是提示所指的语感。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Choose the option that best matches the indicated meaning and tone. This tests the intended nuance; an alternative may be grammatical in another context without expressing that nuance here.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 照理不应该……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: An admonition about the proper course of action.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 从应有做法的角度劝阻独断，用「べきではない」。はずではない表示与预期不符；おそれ要用「おそれがある」；しだい接名词或ます形，「決めるしだいではない」不成立。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: べきではない says you should not decide alone. はずではない means things were not supposed to be so; おそれ takes おそれがある; しだい follows a noun or masu-stem, so 決めるしだいではない is ungrammatical.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 请选最符合提示意思和语气的一项。其他选项换个语境也可能成立，但这里要的是提示所指的语感。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Choose the option that best matches the indicated meaning and tone. This tests the intended nuance; an alternative may be grammatical in another context without expressing that nuance here.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 最好……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Practical advice for this particular problem, without a strong moral obligation.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 面对感冒如何早点好的具体问题，给出“最好早睡”的建议，用「ことだ」。 补充：寝るべきだ也是建议，但更强硬；具体养病建议用ことだ通常更合适。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Target expression: ことだ. Intended meaning: Practical advice for this particular problem, without a strong moral obligation. Compared alternatives: べきだ. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 准是……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: It's probably...

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 「きっと」结合鞋子这个线索，表达很有把握的推断，选に違いない。べきだ表达规范、ことだ表达建议，均不等于这里的行踪推断。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: きっと and the clue provided by the shoes indicate a confident inference, so use に違いない. べきだ expresses an obligation and ことだ gives advice; neither expresses this inference about someone's whereabouts.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 请选最符合提示意思和语气的一项。其他选项换个语境也可能成立，但这里要的是提示所指的语感。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Choose the option that best matches the indicated meaning and tone. This tests the intended nuance; an alternative may be grammatical in another context without expressing that nuance here.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 肯定就是……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: The speaker's emphatic subjective certainty, rather than a mere possibility.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 说话人以强烈、口语的方式断定便宜的名牌货肯定是假的，名词直接接「に決まっている」。 补充：のはずだ表达推断；のおそれがある只说有假货风险；に決まっている是强烈断定，不能把价格低当成已经证实假货。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Target expression: に決まっている. Intended meaning: The speaker's emphatic subjective certainty, rather than a mere possibility. Compared alternatives: のはずだ / のおそれがある. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 肯定就是……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: It's definitely...

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: “他”以很强的主观确信说自己的队伍肯定会赢，用「に決まっている」。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: He is strongly convinced that his team will win. Use に決まっている.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 请选最符合提示意思和语气的一项。其他选项换个语境也可能成立，但这里要的是提示所指的语感。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Choose the option that best matches the indicated meaning and tone. This tests the intended nuance; an alternative may be grammatical in another context without expressing that nuance here.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 恐怕有……风险
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: A formal warning of a possible risk, without claiming certainty.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 这是对道路结冰的正式风险提示，像天气或交通公告，用「おそれがある」。 补充：に決まっている是强烈断定会结冰；おそれがある仅说明风险，天气提醒中更合适。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Target expression: おそれがある. Intended meaning: A formal warning of a possible risk, without claiming certainty. Compared alternatives: に決まっている. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 恐怕有……风险
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: I'm afraid there's a risk.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 产品警示中客观说明可能起火，名词「発火」后用「のおそれがある」。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: A product warning objectively states a risk of fire. Attach のおそれがある to the noun 発火.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 搞不好会……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Maybe...

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 如果继续隐瞒，搞不好会让整个公司失去信誉，用动词ます形词干「失い」接「かねない」。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Continued concealment might cost the whole company its credibility. Attach かねない to the masu-stem 失い.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 搞不好会……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Maybe...

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.zh: 警告鲁莽驾驶可能酿成重大事故，「起こし」后接「かねない」。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.14-judgm.en: Reckless driving may cause a serious accident. Attach かねない to 起こし.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 「不管……都……」——条件怎么变，结果不变。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: “Regardless of…” — change the condition, the result stays.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 前项的差别、条件或选项不影响后项，所有情况得到同样结果。常接「年齢」「性別」「天候」「理由」这类可变的分类。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Differences, conditions or options in the first half make no difference to the second, and every case gets the same result. It takes variables such as age, sex, weather or reason.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 名词／相对词组／动词辞书形・ない形＋にかかわらず
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Noun / paired terms / dictionary or ない-form + にかかわらず

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 和 Day 8 的「にもかかわらず」只差一个「も」，意思完全不同：有「も」是“尽管 A 居然 B”，没有「も」是“不管 A，B 都一样”。考试最爱在这里设陷阱。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: One も separates it from Day 8's にもかかわらず, and the meaning flips: with も it means despite A, B happened; without も it means whatever A, B is the same. Exams love to hide the trap here.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不管年龄多大，任何人都可以报名。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Anyone may apply, regardless of age.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不管天气如何，比赛照常举行。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: The match will go ahead whatever the weather.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不管有没有理由，都不允许缺席。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Absence is not permitted, with or without a reason.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 「不论……一概……」——正式宣告不作限制。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: “Irrespective of…” — a formal declaration that a criterion does not apply.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 正式地宣布某个分类标准不作限制，凡符合其他条件的人或情况一概适用。招聘、活动、公告里最常见。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: It formally announces that a category is not a restriction, so anyone or anything meeting the other conditions qualifies. It is most common in recruitment, events and notices.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 名词＋を問わず
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Noun + を問わず

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 意思接近「にかかわらず」，但更书面、更像招聘广告。常见搭配是固定的：年齢・性別・国籍・経験の有無を問わず。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Close to にかかわらず but more formal and more like a job ad. The collocations are fixed: 年齢・性別・国籍・経験の有無を問わず.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不论有无经验，一概可以报名。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: You may apply whether or not you have experience.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不分性别，很多人参加了。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Many people took part, regardless of gender.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不论星期几，随时联系我。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Contact me any day of the week.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 「……先不说」——A 暂时不评价，重点转到 B。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: “Setting A aside…” — A goes unjudged while B takes the focus.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 暂时不评价 A，或不把 A 当作当前重点，转而强调更值得关注的 B。多用于比较评价：A 姑且不论，B 至少如何。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: A is left unjudged or off the agenda while B, the more important point, is emphasised. It usually compares: whatever A may be, B at least is such and such.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 名词／普通形＋の＋はともかく
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Noun / plain form + の + はともかく

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 和「はさておき」比，它更常带评价：“价格先不说，质量很好”。はさておき则更像主持人把话题挪开，不一定要比较优劣。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Compared with はさておき it more often carries an evaluation: never mind the price, the quality is good. はさておき is more like a host moving a topic aside and need not compare better or worse.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 价格先不说，质量确实很好。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Never mind the price — the quality is excellent.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 卖相先不说，味道我保证。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Never mind how it looks; I guarantee the taste.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 结果先不说，你已经很努力了。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Whatever the result, you worked hard.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 「……先放一边」——把话题挪开，进正题。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: “Let's leave A aside” — move the topic and get to business.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 有意识地把当前话题 A 暂时搁置，为更重要或更正式的话题 B 腾出位置。话题操作的意味很强。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: The current topic A is deliberately parked so that a more important or more formal topic B can take its place. The sense of managing the conversation is strong.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 名词／普通形＋の＋はさておき
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Noun / plain form + の + はさておき

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 典型场景是「冗談はさておき、本題に入りましょう」。它不一定要比较 A 和 B 哪个更好，只是把 A 挪开——这点和「はともかく」不同。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: The typical setting is 冗談はさておき、本題に入りましょう. It need not weigh A against B at all, only move A aside, which is where it differs from はともかく.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 玩笑先放一边，我们进入正题吧。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Jokes aside, let us get to the point.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 费用先放一边，先考虑安全性吧。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Let us put cost aside and think about safety first.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 名字先不管，这道菜很好吃。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Never mind the name — this dish is delicious.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 「不过就是……」——把被看重的压回它真实的分量。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: “Nothing more than…” — presses something back down to its real weight.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 把对方可能看得过重的人、事、数量或判断压回有限范围：它没有超出 A。带弱化语气，常用于自谦或降温。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: It presses a person, thing, quantity or judgement that may have been overrated back into a limited range: it goes no further than A. The tone deflates, and it serves for modesty or cooling things down.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 名词／普通形＋にすぎない
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Noun / plain form + にすぎない

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 方向是弱化：“别把它想得太重，不过就是 A”。和「にほかならない」正好相反——那个是强化与聚焦：“本质上正是 A”。同一件事用两者说，评价完全相反。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: It deflates: do not take it too seriously, it is only A. It is the opposite of にほかならない, which intensifies and focuses: it is precisely A. The same fact takes either, with opposite evaluations.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 这不过就是我个人的看法。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: This is nothing more than my personal opinion.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 他不过还是个新人。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: He is still only a newcomer.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 原因不过是个误会。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: The cause was nothing more than a misunderstanding.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 「说白了就是……／正是……」——排除别的解释，锁定本质。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: “Nothing other than…” — rules out other explanations and pins the essence.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 把事物的真正原因、核心或本质精确锁定为 A。语气坚定，常用于议论、演讲、结论句。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: It pins the true cause, core or essence precisely on A. The tone is firm, and it belongs to argument, speeches and conclusions.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 名词＋にほかならない；原因句常用「～のは、～からにほかならない」
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Noun + にほかならない; causal sentences often take ～のは、～からにほかならない

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 和「にすぎない」是一对反向表达：一个限制价值（不过是），一个强调本质（正是）。判断标准是说话人想把这件事说小还是说重。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: It is the mirror of にすぎない: one limits the value (only), the other stresses the essence (precisely). The test is whether the speaker wants to play the thing down or play it up.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 成功的原因，说白了正是每天的努力。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: The reason for the success is nothing other than daily effort.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 他生气，说到底是因为他想被信任。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: He was angry for no other reason than wanting to be trusted.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 这个结果，正是准备不足的体现。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: This result is nothing but a symptom of inadequate preparation.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 请选最符合提示意思和语气的一项。其他选项换个语境也可能成立，但这里要的是提示所指的语感。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Choose the option that best matches the indicated meaning and tone. This tests the intended nuance; an alternative may be grammatical in another context without expressing that nuance here.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不管……都……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: A condition that makes no difference to eligibility.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 有没有经验不影响起点，所有人都从同一基础课开始。前面是完整问句形式，用「にかかわらず」。 补充：はともかく是暂时不讨论经验；にかかわらず明确表示不把经验作为分班条件。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Target expression: にかかわらず. Intended meaning: A condition that makes no difference to eligibility. Compared alternatives: はともかく. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 请选最符合提示意思和语气的一项。其他选项换个语境也可能成立，但这里要的是提示所指的语感。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Choose the option that best matches the indicated meaning and tone. This tests the intended nuance; an alternative may be grammatical in another context without expressing that nuance here.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不管……都……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: A condition that makes no difference to the decision.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 下雨还是不下雨都不影响比赛举行，相对条件后用「にかかわらず」。 补充：はさておき可先搁置天气话题再说明比赛安排；にかかわらず明确表示天气不影响决定。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Target expression: にかかわらず. Intended meaning: A condition that makes no difference to the decision. Compared alternatives: はさておき. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 请选最符合提示意思和语气的一项。其他选项换个语境也可能成立，但这里要的是提示所指的语感。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Choose the option that best matches the indicated meaning and tone. This tests the intended nuance; an alternative may be grammatical in another context without expressing that nuance here.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不论……一概……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: A formal statement that nationality is not a restriction.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 比赛规则正式声明不限国籍，名词「国籍」后用公告式的「を問わず」。 补充：はともかく可暂不讨论国籍；を問わず直接说明没有国籍限制。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Target expression: を問わず. Intended meaning: A formal statement that nationality is not a restriction. Compared alternatives: はともかく. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 请选最符合提示意思和语气的一项。其他选项换个语境也可能成立，但这里要的是提示所指的语感。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Choose the option that best matches the indicated meaning and tone. This tests the intended nuance; an alternative may be grammatical in another context without expressing that nuance here.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不论……一概……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: A formal statement that age and gender are not restrictions.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 招聘信息中正式表示不论年龄和性别，「を問わず」最符合公告语气。 补充：はさておき可先放下年龄性别的话题；を問わず更明确是招聘条件不限制这些因素。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Target expression: を問わず. Intended meaning: A formal statement that age and gender are not restrictions. Compared alternatives: はさておき. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: ……先不说
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: I'm not going to say anything.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 设计好不好暂且不评价，转而强调电脑的性能好。题干已有「は」，补「ともかく」。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Designs are not yet evaluated, instead they emphasize the performance of computers. The subject has been "は" and is supplemented by "ともかく. "

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: ……先不说
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: I'm not going to say anything.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 方法正不正确先不说，至少结果已经出现。题干已有「は」，补「ともかく」。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: The method is not correct, at least the results have already appeared. The subject has been "は" and added "ともかく " .

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: ……先放一边
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: ...and put it aside first.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 主动把费用话题暂时搁置，把讨论转到能否实现上，用「はさておき」。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Take the initiative to put the issue of costs on hold and move the discussion to whether it is possible to do so, using "はさておき " .

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: ……先放一边
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: ...and put it aside first.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 把开场铺垫暂时放到一边，要求直接说结论，是主动转换话题的「はさておき」。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Putting the opening mat aside for the time being and asking for a direct conclusion is " はさておき " , which changes the subject.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不过就是……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: It's just...

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 「伝えたにすぎない」把行为限定为转达。にほかならない通常接名词／名词化表达，如「伝えただけということにほかならない」，不能用无名词化的动词句机械替换。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: 伝えたにすぎない limits the action to passing on a message. にほかならない normally follows a noun or nominalized expression, such as 伝えただけということにほかならない. Do not mechanically replace it after a non-nominalized verb clause.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 请选最符合提示意思和语气的一项。其他选项换个语境也可能成立，但这里要的是提示所指的语感。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Choose the option that best matches the indicated meaning and tone. This tests the intended nuance; an alternative may be grammatical in another context without expressing that nuance here.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 不过就是……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Only a personal opinion, downplaying its authority.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 将发言限定为个人意见，不要当成组织立场，是弱化的「にすぎない」。 补充：にほかならない强调“本质就是个人意见”；にすぎない弱化意见的权威与代表性。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Target expression: にすぎない. Intended meaning: Only a personal opinion, downplaying its authority. Compared alternatives: にほかならない. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 正是……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: That's right.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 「～のは、～からにほかならない」强调成功的真正原因。这里需要完整的原因形式，不能把「のは」与一个孤立的名词原因机械拼起来。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: In ～のは、～からにほかならない, the clause before から states the real reason. A complete reason clause is needed; an isolated noun cannot simply be inserted into that position.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 请选最符合提示意思和语气的一项。其他选项换个语境也可能成立，但这里要的是提示所指的语感。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: Choose the option that best matches the indicated meaning and tone. This tests the intended nuance; an alternative may be grammatical in another context without expressing that nuance here.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 说白了就是……
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: An emphatic identification of the essential cause.

nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.zh: 强调失败的本质正是准备不足造成的，用「にほかならない」。はさておき、にかかわらず、に先立って后面都必须再接句子，不能结句。
nihongo-noryoku-shiken-n2-bunpo.15-scope.en: にほかならない: the failure is nothing other than the result of poor preparation. はさておき, にかかわらず and に先立って all need a following clause and cannot end the sentence.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.0.zh: 一类动词（五段）：词尾在う段。以る结尾也可能是一类，例如帰る、入る、走る、切る、知る、要る。不能只看到る就判定二类。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.0.en: Group 1 (godan): the final kana has a u-vowel. Some verbs ending in る also belong here: 帰る, 入る, 走る, 切る, 知る and 要る. A final る alone does not identify Group 2.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.0.zh: 二类动词（一段）：辞书形通常以「い段＋る」或「え段＋る」结尾，变形时去掉る。食べる、見る、起きる、借りる都是二类；记单词时一起记类别。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.0.en: Group 2 (ichidan): dictionary forms usually end in an i- or e-vowel plus る. Remove る when conjugating. 食べる, 見る, 起きる and 借りる are Group 2. Learn the group with each verb.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.0.zh: 三类动词（不规则）：する、来る，以及勉強する等「名词＋する」。来る的读音会变：くる、きます、こない，不能只看汉字。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.0.en: Group 3 (irregular): する, 来る and compounds such as 勉強する. The reading of 来る changes: くる, きます, こない. The kanji alone does not show the change.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.0.zh: 只知道「～ます」时，先查回辞书形和类别。「切ります」来自一类切る；「借ります」来自二类借りる，两者不能套用同一规则。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.0.en: If you only know the ます form, check the dictionary form and group first. 切ります comes from Group 1 切る, but 借ります comes from Group 2 借りる. They follow different rules.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 「未然形」「連用形」这些名字来自日本学校的语法，JLPT 的语法书和词典也常这么叫。教材（みんなの日本語等）习惯按用途叫「ない形」「ます形」——两套名字指的是同一批词尾变化，先记住对照表，再看后面每一种形。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Names such as 未然形 and 連用形 come from the grammar taught in Japanese schools, and JLPT references and dictionaries use them too. Textbooks like みんなの日本語 name the same endings by their use (ない形, ます形). Learn the mapping first, then the forms.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 以「書く」为例：未然形＝書か（接ない）／書こ（接う）→ ない形・意向形，第 09・12 項；連用形＝書き（接ます・て・た）→ 第 05・06・07 項；終止形＝書く（结句）、連体形＝書く（接名词）→ 辞書形，第 03 項；仮定形＝書け（接ば）→ ば形，第 14 項；命令形＝書け → 第 13 項。六个形在本单元各自成页，这一页只用来看清两套名字怎么对上。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: With 書く: 未然形 = 書か (before ない) / 書こ (before う) → the ない form and the volitional, items 09 and 12; 連用形 = 書き (before ます, て, た) → items 05, 06 and 07; 終止形 = 書く (ends a sentence) and 連体形 = 書く (before a noun) → the dictionary form, item 03; 仮定形 = 書け (before ば) → the ば form, item 14; 命令形 = 書け → item 13. Each shape has its own page here; this page only maps the two sets of names.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 辞书形是词典里的形式，也叫原形；不是一律去ます后加る。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: The dictionary form is the form used as a dictionary headword. Do not simply replace every ます with る.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 「見ます→見る」不是一类变化。接こと、前に、ように等时，要确认句型要求的是辞书形还是普通形。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: 見ます → 見る is a Group 2 change. Check whether the sentence pattern requires the dictionary form specifically or any plain form.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 睡觉前刷牙。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: I brush my teeth before going to bed.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 去ます，把最后一个い段假名改为同一行的う段。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: Remove ます, then change the final i-vowel kana to the u-vowel kana in the same row.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 去ます，直接加る；不要再把词干里的假名改成う段。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: Remove ます and add る. Do not alter the last kana of the stem.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 不按前两类推算，记住固定对应。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: Memorize the irregular equivalents.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.3.zh: 連用形接「ます」，也接「て」「た」「たい」「ながら」。一类换到イ段（書く→書き），二类去掉る（食べる→食べ），する→し，来る→き。注意て形还有促音便、イ音便，光看連用形推不出来（書く→書いて）。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.3.en: The 連用形 takes ます, and also て, た, たい, ながら. Group 1 shifts to the i-row (書く→書き), Group 2 drops る (食べる→食べ), する→し, 来る→き. The て form also has sound changes, so 連用形 alone does not predict it (書く→書いて).

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.zh: 先做出ます词干，再根据肯定、否定及时间选择词尾。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.en: Build the stem first, then choose the ending for polarity and tense.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.zh: 「ます」既可表示习惯，也可表示将来，时间由语境决定。「ましょう」用ます词干＋ましょう；邀请「ませんか」用ます词干＋ませんか。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.en: ます can express habits or future events depending on context. For a suggestion, attach ましょう to the stem; for an invitation, attach ませんか.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.zh: 昨天没有学习，今天会学习。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.en: I did not study yesterday. I will study today.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.zh: 辞书形最后的う段假名改为同一行い段，再加ます。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.en: Change the final u-vowel kana to its i-vowel counterpart and add ます.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.zh: 去掉辞书形的る，加ます。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.en: Remove the final る and add ます.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.zh: 记住する与来る的词干。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.4.en: Use the irregular stems of する and 来る.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.zh: 一类不能统一去ます加て，要从辞书形词尾判断音便；二类和三类另外处理。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.en: For Group 1, the dictionary ending determines the sound change. Group 2 and Group 3 follow separate rules.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.zh: 特例：行く→行って，不是行いて。用ます形记忆时，必须先知道类别：帰ります→帰って；借ります→借りて。て形本身不决定过去或现在。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.en: Exception: 行く → 行って, not 行いて. If starting from ます, identify the group first: 帰ります → 帰って, but 借ります → 借りて. The て form itself does not mark past versus present.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.zh: 请打开窗户。我现在正在看书。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.en: Please open the window. I am reading a book now.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.zh: 词尾变成って。这里只包含一类的る结尾动词。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.en: Replace the ending with って. The る rule here applies only to Group 1.
Replace the ending with んで.
Usually replace く with いて.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.zh: 把ぐ变成いで；注意用で，不是て。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.en: Replace ぐ with いで, using で rather than て.
Remove る and add て.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.zh: 行く不按「く→いて」变化，要单独记为行って。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.5.en: 行く does not follow the usual く → いて pattern. Memorize 行って.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.6.zh: 先掌握て形，再把末尾的て换成た、で换成だ。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.6.en: First build the て form, then replace final て with た or final で with だ.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.6.zh: 行く→行った。た形可表示过去，也用于「たことがある」「たり」「たほうがいい」等结构；不能把所有た形都简单译成“过去”。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.6.en: 行く becomes 行った. The た form also appears in たことがある, たり and たほうがいい; it does not always describe a past event.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.6.zh: う・つ・る→った；む・ぶ・ぬ→んだ；く→いた；ぐ→いだ；す→した。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.6.en: Use った for う・つ・る, んだ for む・ぶ・ぬ, いた for く, いだ for ぐ, and した for す.
Remove る and add た.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.6.zh: する→した；来る→来た，读きた。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.6.en: Use した for する and 来た (きた) for 来る.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.6.zh: 行く的过去形是行った，不是行いた。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.6.en: The past form of 行く is 行った, not 行いた.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.7.zh: 未然形是「还没发生」的那半截：后面接ない、ぬ、う・よう、れる・られる、せる・させる。一类把词尾换到ア段（書く→書か、買う→買わ），要接「う」时换オ段（書こう）；二类去掉る（食べる→食べ）；する→し／さ／せ，来る→こ。这里只认形：れる・られる（受身）、せる・させる（使役）在第 16・17・18 項才展开。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.7.en: The 未然形 is the "not yet happened" stem: it takes ない, ぬ, う/よう, れる/られる, せる/させる. Group 1 shifts the final kana to the a-row (書く→書か, 買う→買わ) and to the o-row before う (書こう); Group 2 drops る (食べる→食べ); する→し/さ/せ, 来る→こ. Only the shape belongs here: れる/られる (passive) and せる/させる (causative) are explained in items 16, 17 and 18.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.8.zh: 一类换あ段，二类去る，三类单独记。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.8.en: Group 1 changes to an a-vowel; Group 2 drops る; Group 3 is irregular.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.8.zh: ある的否定是ない，不是あらない。接「なければ」「なくても」时，把整个ない换掉：書かない→書かなければ／書かなくても。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.8.en: The negative of ある is ない, not あらない. To build なければ or なくても, replace the whole ない: 書かない → 書かなければ／書かなくても.
I intend not to go to school tomorrow.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.8.zh: 词尾う段改成同一行あ段，加ない；但词尾う要变わ。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.8.en: Change the final u-vowel kana to its a-vowel counterpart and add ない. Final う changes to わ.
Remove る and add ない.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.9.zh: 动词普通形包括非过去肯定、非过去否定、过去肯定、过去否定四种。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.9.en: A verb has four basic plain forms: affirmative non-past, negative non-past, affirmative past and negative past.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.9.zh: 动词普通形后不加だ：行くと思う，不是行くだと思う。名词和な形容词的普通形规则不同，不要套到动词上。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.9.en: Do not add だ after a plain verb: 行くと思う, not 行くだと思う. Nouns and な-adjectives have different plain-form rules.
Tanaka said they would not come tomorrow.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.9.zh: 依次使用辞书形、ない形、た形、なかった形；先确定要表达的时间和肯定／否定。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.9.en: Choose the dictionary, ない, た or なかった form according to tense and polarity.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.9.zh: 接と思う、と言う、し或修饰名词时，保留所需的普通形，再接后面的词。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.9.en: For と思う, と言う, し or noun modification, choose the appropriate plain form before attaching the rest.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 表达能力或条件上的可能；不是把所有动词都加られる。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: This form expresses ability or the possibility of an action. Not every verb takes られる.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 本页使用教材标准形式「食べられる／来られる」。口语的食べれる、来れる属于ら抜き。見える／聞こえる通常表示自然看见／听见，不能当作見る／聞く的机械可能形。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: This guide uses standard textbook 食べられる／来られる. Colloquial 食べれる／来れる omit ら. 見える／聞こえる usually describe something being visible/audible; they are not the mechanically formed potentials of 見る／聞く.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 我能读日文报纸。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: I can read Japanese newspapers.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 词尾う段变同一行え段，再加る。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Change the final u-vowel kana to its e-vowel counterpart and add る.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 去る，加られる。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Remove る and add られる.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: する→できる；来る→来られる，读こられる。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Use できる for する and 来られる (こられる) for 来る.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 可能形变成二类方式继续活用：去る后接ない／ます。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Conjugate the resulting potential verb like Group 2: remove る before ない or ます.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 普通体意向形常接と思う、と思っている、とする。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: The plain volitional form often precedes と思う, と思っている or とする.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 礼貌的提议用ます词干＋ましょう。書く→書こう，不能从書きます直接拼成書きよう。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: For a polite suggestion, use the ます stem plus ましょう. 書く becomes 書こう, not 書きよう.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 我打算周末在图书馆学习。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: I am planning to study at the library this weekend.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 词尾う段变同一行お段，加う。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Change the final u-vowel kana to its o-vowel counterpart and add う.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 去る，加よう。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Remove る and add よう.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: する→しよう；来る→来よう，读こよう。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Use しよう for する and 来よう (こよう) for 来る.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 命令形和禁止形是两套规则。语气强，先学会辨认标语和紧急指示。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Commands and prohibitions use different rules. Their tone is strong; learn to recognize them in signs and urgent instructions.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 帰れ是命令，帰れる是可能；食べるな是禁止，不是食べない。礼貌请求通常用てください／ないでください。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: 帰れ is a command; 帰れる is potential. 食べるな is a prohibition, distinct from the negative 食べない. Polite requests normally use てください／ないでください.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 不要在这里停车。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Do not park here.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 词尾う段改同一行え段，不加る。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Change the final u-vowel kana to its e-vowel counterpart; do not add る.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 去る，加ろ。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Remove る and add ろ.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 记住しろ／せよ和来い。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Use the irregular しろ／せよ and 来い.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 辞书形原样保留，直接加な。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Keep the dictionary form unchanged and add な.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 肯定动词和否定动词的变化入口不同。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Affirmative and negative conditions start from different forms.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 「行けば」不是「行きば」。ば、たら、なら、とは不能随意互换；这里先解决形态，具体条件语感看本课文法。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Use 行けば, not 行きば. ば, たら, なら and と are not interchangeable; consult the lesson explanation for their differences in meaning.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 每天练习的话，就会进步。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: If you practice every day, you will improve.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 词尾う段改え段，加ば。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Change the final u-vowel kana to its e-vowel counterpart and add ば.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 去る，加れば。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Remove る and add れば.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: する→すれば；来る→来れば，读くれば。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Use すれば for する and 来れば (くれば) for 来る.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 先变ない形，再把ない改成なければ。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Build the ない form, then replace ない with なければ.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 不要直接在辞书形后加たら；先完成た形或なかった形。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Do not attach たら directly to the dictionary form. Build the た or なかった form first.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 形式里有た，不等于事情已经发生：明日雨が降ったら说的是明天的条件。读んだら保留浊音だ。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: The た in this form does not mean the event has happened: 明日雨が降ったら describes a condition tomorrow. 読んだら keeps voiced だ.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 回到家以后，请打电话。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Please call when you get home.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 各类动词先变た形，再加ら。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: For every group, build the た form and add ら.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 先变ない，再变なかった，最后加ら。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Build ない, change it to なかった, then add ら.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 先变被动动词，再处理句子里谁受到谁的动作。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: First form the passive verb, then identify who is affected by whose action.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 二类和来る的可能形、被动形同形，要靠主语、助词和语境判断。一类可以直接对比：書ける＝能写，書かれる＝被写。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Group 2 and 来る have identical potential and passive forms; use subjects, particles and context to distinguish them. For Group 1: 書ける means can write, while 書かれる is passive.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 我受到了老师的表扬。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: I was praised by my teacher.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 词尾う段改あ段，加れる；う→わ。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Change the final u-vowel kana to its a-vowel counterpart and add れる; う becomes わ.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 去る，加られる。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Remove る and add られる.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: する→される；来る→来られる，读こられる。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Use される for する and 来られる (こられる) for 来る.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 被动形形成后按二类继续变。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Conjugate the resulting passive like Group 2.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 使役可以表达要求、允许或引发某种反应，不能只机械译成“强迫”。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: The causative can express instructions, permission or causing a reaction; it does not always mean forcing someone.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 注意三种不同形式：食べられる（被动／可能）、食べさせる（使役）、食べさせられる（使役受身）。句中动作对象仍用を时，被使役的人常用に。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Distinguish 食べられる (passive/potential), 食べさせる (causative) and 食べさせられる (causative-passive). When を marks the action’s object, the person made or allowed to act commonly takes に.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 老师让学生写了作文。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: The teacher had the students write an essay.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 词尾う段改あ段，加せる；う→わ。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Change the final u-vowel kana to its a-vowel counterpart and add せる; う becomes わ.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 去る，加させる。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Remove る and add させる.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: する→させる；来る→来させる，读こさせる。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Use させる for する and 来させる (こさせる) for 来る.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 使役动词按二类处理：去末尾る，加て，才能接ください／もらう／いただく。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Treat the causative as Group 2: remove final る and add て before ください, もらう or いただく.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 先做使役形，再把使役动词变成被动形。先掌握完整形式，再记常见缩略。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Build the causative first, then make that verb passive. Learn the full forms before the common contractions.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 主语是被要求做动作的人。使役＋てもらう是“获得允许／请对方让自己做”，不要与使役受身混为一谈。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: The subject is the person made to act. Causative + てもらう expresses receiving permission or arranging to be allowed to act; it is not the causative-passive.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 我被老师要求写了作文。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: I was made to write an essay by my teacher.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: あ段词干＋せる，再把せる变せられる。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Use the a-vowel stem plus せる, then change せる to せられる.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 多数非す结尾的一类动词可把せられる缩成される。す结尾不按此缩。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Many Group 1 verbs not ending in す shorten せられる to される. Do not apply this contraction to verbs ending in す.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 去る，加させられる。不要缩成さされる。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Remove る and add させられる. Do not shorten it to さされる.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: する→させられる；来る→来させられる，读こさせられる。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Use させられる for する and 来させられる (こさせられる) for 来る.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 先变出ない形，再按表达目的选择后续形式。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Build the ない form first, then choose the ending that fits the meaning.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: ないで与なくて不是仅有书面口语差别；句子关系不同。ずにはいられない保留ずに，再加はいられない。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: ないで and なくて are not simply informal versus formal alternatives: they express different relationships. For ずにはいられない, keep ずに and add はいられない.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 没吃早饭就去了学校。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: I went to school without eating breakfast.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 保留ない，直接加で，常表示“不做前项而做后项”，也可接ください。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Keep ない and add で, often for doing something without doing another action, or before ください.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 把ない的い变くて，常用于否定原因或连接否定内容。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Replace the final い of ない with くて, often for a negative cause or to connect negative content.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 去ない，加ずに；但する不是しずに，而是せずに。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Remove ない and add ずに. For する, use せずに, not しずに.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 尊敬语抬高动作主体。先确认是谁做动作，再选结构。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Honorific language elevates the person performing the action. Identify that person before choosing a pattern.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 不要用尊敬语抬高自己的动作。「お読みください」是お＋ます词干＋ください，不是お読んでください。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Do not use honorific verbs to elevate your own actions. お読みください uses お + ます stem + ください, not お読んでください.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 老师已经回去了。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: The teacher has already gone home.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 先去ます，再放进お～になる；句末可把なる变成なります。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Remove ます and insert the stem into お～になる; なる can then become polite なります.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 形态按被动形规则，但此处表示尊敬，要靠语境与被动区分。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Use the passive conjugation pattern, but interpret it as honorific in the appropriate context.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.zh: 常用动词有专用尊敬语，不是机械加お；部分ます形还有特殊词干。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.1.en: Common verbs have special honorific equivalents. Some also have irregular ます stems.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 谦逊语用于自己或己方的动作，以尊重动作涉及的对方；不是所有动作都能机械套用。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: Humble language describes your own or your in-group’s action with respect to its recipient or other relevant person. The pattern cannot be applied mechanically to every action.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 尊敬语描述应尊敬的人的动作；谦逊语描述自己／己方的动作。不要把「先生が拝見します」当作尊敬表达。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: Honorific verbs describe the respected person’s action; humble verbs describe your own or your in-group’s action. 先生が拝見します is not an honorific way to describe the teacher looking.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 我来帮您拿行李。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: I will carry your luggage.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 去ます，加お和する；再把する变成します。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: Remove ます, add お before the stem and する after it, then make する polite if needed.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 案内、説明等使用ご～する；不是把每个する动词都加ご。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: Words such as 案内 and 説明 take ご～する; not every する compound permits ご.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 专用谦逊、丁重表达需要分别记忆。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: Memorize special humble and courteous equivalents individually.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 缩略是在完整接续已经形成后发生的，不是新的动词类别。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: Contractions happen after the full construction is formed; they do not create a new verb group.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 先学会完整形式及意思；正式写作和教材答题按要求使用完整形式，不要把缩略直接当成唯一标准答案。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: Learn the full form and meaning first. Use full forms when formal writing or textbook exercises require them; contractions are not the only correct forms.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 把作业忘了。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: I forgot my homework.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: 口语中常省去いる的い；でいる同理。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: In casual speech, the い of いる is often omitted, also after で.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: てしまう常缩为ちゃう，でしまう常缩为じゃう。过去式再把う变った。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: てしまう often contracts to ちゃう, and でしまう to じゃう. For the past, change final う to った.

jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.zh: ておく常缩为とく，でおく常缩为どく。
jlpt-n5-doshi-no-katsuyo.verbs.grammar.2.en: ておく often contracts to とく; でおく to どく.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.0.zh: 这里的「って」相当于提示话题的「は」，用于口语。ストレス、リラックス、カラオケ、ロック・フェスティバル都是片假名词。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.0.en: "って" here is equivalent to "は" for the subject. ストレス, リラックス, カラオケ, ロック, フェスティバル are katakana words.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.1.zh: 「でしょう」的普通体，用于推测或委婉表达看法。不是表示过去的形式。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.1.en: The plain counterpart of でしょう, used for conjecture or a tentative opinion. It does not mark the past.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.2.zh: 「のでしょうか」的普通体，常见于书面语，用来委婉提出疑问，也可表示思考、自问。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.2.en: The plain counterpart of のでしょうか, often used in writing for a tentative question, reflection or self-questioning.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.3.zh: 根据常识或已知情况，强烈否定某种可能。句中若已有否定形式，整体可能表达强烈肯定。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.3.en: There is a strong rejection of a possibility based on common sense or known circumstances. If there is a negative form in the sentence, it may be a strong affirmation overall.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.4.zh: 「わけではない」表示“并不是……”，不一定全盘否定；「毎日するわけではない」是“并非每天都做”。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.4.en: わけではない rejects an inference or generalization without necessarily denying everything. 毎日するわけではない means that the action is not done every day.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.5.zh: 替换发生在修饰名词的从句内部，不适用于所有「が」。例如独立句「私が行きます」不能直接改成「私の行きます」。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.5.en: The replacement applies inside a noun-modifying clause, not to every が. The independent sentence 私が行きます cannot simply become 私の行きます.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.6.zh: 突出说话人认为最重要、最值得强调的部分。「今度こそ」常表达“这次一定要”的决心。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.6.en: Highlights what the speaker considers most important. 今度こそ often expresses determination to succeed this time.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.7.zh: 括号内是教材展示的省略部分。省略后仍需保证意思清楚，不能机械删除所有重复动词。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.7.en: The brackets are omitted from the presentation of the educational material. It is still necessary to make sure that the meaning is clear and that all duplicate verbs cannot be deleted mechanically.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.8.zh: 本课的「より」单独作副词，表示程度进一步提高。注意与「AよりB」中表示比较基准的「より」区分。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.1.grammar.8.en: Here より is an adverb meaning a greater degree. Distinguish it from the comparison marker より in AよりB.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.0.zh: 表示名称、具体内容或定义。口语常用「っていう」或「って」。名词／な形容词谓语表达内容时保留「だ」，如「冬は暖冬だという予想」。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.0.en: Introduces a name, content or definition. In conversation, という often becomes っていう or って. Keep だ in noun/na-adjective predicates expressing content, as in 冬は暖冬だという予想.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.1.zh: 以某事物为最高程度的比较基准。「いない」用于人、动物等有生命的存在；「ない」用于事物或情况。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.1.en: The highest level of comparison is based on something. " いない" is used for the existence of humans, animals, etc.; "ない " is used for things or situations.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.2.zh: 通过具体例子或比喻说明程度。「ぐらい／くらい」常用于口语。本课将「死ぬほど」这类极端比喻与一般程度表达区分，练习中用「死ぬほど疲れた」。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.2.en: Uses an example or comparison to express degree. ぐらい／くらい are common in conversation. This lesson distinguishes extreme comparisons such as 死ぬほど from ordinary degree expressions and practices 死ぬほど疲れた.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.3.zh: 既可表示站在某人的立场看问题，也可表示以某种线索为依据作判断。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.3.en: It can be expressed either to look at the issue in a person ' s position or to judge on the basis of certain leads.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.4.zh: 把两个问题或关注点作比较。前项常有「どんな」「いくら」等疑问词，用「か」把疑问小句嵌入句中。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.4.en: Compares two questions or concerns. The first clause often contains a question word such as どんな or いくら and is embedded with か.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.5.zh: 本项为补充学习内容。0也读れい，4也读し，7也读しち，9也读く；本练习优先使用ゼロ・よん・なな・きゅう，便于清楚报数。数字与日期、时间、量词搭配时可能有不同读法，如四月（しがつ）、四時（よじ），不能机械套用。先看数字读一遍，再点击发音核对；也可遮住数字，只听读音后写下数字。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.2.grammar.5.en: Supplementary number practice. 0 also has the reading れい, 4 has し, 7 has しち, and 9 has く. This exercise uses ゼロ・よん・なな・きゅう for clarity. Dates, times and counters may require different readings, such as 四月（しがつ）and 四時（よじ）. Read each number, then check its pronunciation; alternatively, cover the number and write what you hear.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.0.zh: 以前面的事件为起点，表示状态持续或动作反复发生到现在或某个参照时间。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.0.en: Start with the preceding events, indicating that the state continues or is repeated to the present or at a given reference time.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.1.zh: 「何回も・何人も・何年も」强调次数、人数或时间之多。「何人か」表示不确定的若干人，通常不强调数量大。不要把「何～も」与「何も～ない」混同。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.1.en: 何回も, 何人も and 何年も emphasize a large number of times, people or years. 何人か means an unspecified few people, not necessarily many. Distinguish 何～も from 何も～ない (nothing / not anything).

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.2.zh: 文章中的「こ・そ」可指前文内容；「こ」常将内容作为自己身边或自己关注的事来谈。会话中，在回指已知事物时，双方都知道的常用「あ」，只有一方知道、另一方刚听说的常用「そ」。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.2.en: The article 'こ . そ ' may refer to the previous text; 'こ' often refers to it as a matter of personal or personal concern. In sessions, when referring to what is known, both parties know the usual 'あ' and only one party knows, and the other has just heard, the usual 'そ '

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.3.zh: 本课用来根据事实引出结论或换一种说法解释。不应与表示传闻的「ということだ」混淆。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.3.en: This lesson is used to draw conclusions or a different interpretation based on facts. It should not be confused with the anecdotal "ということだ " .

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.4.zh: 事情已经很明显，或不值得特意采取某个行动。「までもなく」用于连接后文；常见「言うまでもなく」（不言而喻）。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.4.en: It has become clear that something is not worth taking. " までもなく " is used to connect to the back; commonly " 言うまでもなく " (specify).

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.5.zh: 书面表达，相当于「疑问词＋名词＋でも」。列举两项时表示两者均适用。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.5.en: Written expression, equivalent to "question word + noun + でも " . The listing indicates that both apply.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.6.zh: 本课重点不是“正在移动”，而是已移动并处于结果状态。例如「会場に行っている」表示已经去了会场。也可表示恢复等变化的结果状态，如「元の状態に戻っている」。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.3.grammar.6.en: The focus is the resulting state after movement, rather than movement in progress. 会場に行っている means that someone has already gone to the venue. 元の状態に戻っている describes a restored state.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.0.zh: 前项发生后，紧接着出现意料之外的变化。后项通常不接说话人的意志、请求或命令。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.0.en: The latter does not normally follow the will, request or order of the person who speaks.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.1.zh: 「だす」可表示向外出现，也可表示突然开始。「込む」可表示向内移动，也可表示深入、充分地做某事。不同复合动词的意思需结合词汇学习。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.1.en: だす can express outward movement or a sudden beginning. 込む can express inward movement or doing something deeply or thoroughly. Learn each compound verb in context.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.2.zh: 区分三个意思：共同做事、同时进行两件事、一方变化伴随另一方变化。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.2.en: Three meanings are distinguished: to do things together, to do two things simultaneously, and one change with the other.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.3.zh: 例如「学校で生活する→学校での生活」。本课不使用「がの」「をの」；不能机械地给所有助词加の。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.3.en: For example: 学校で生活する→学校での生活. This lesson does not use がの or をの; do not mechanically add の to every particle.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.4.zh: 表示移动或某个过程尚未完成的阶段。「途中で」常用来说明在这个阶段发生了另一件事。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.4.en: Indicates the stage at which a move or a process has not been completed. " 途中で" is often used to describe another event that occurred at this stage.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.5.zh: 教材列出的身体感觉词：むずむず（痒酥酥）、どきどき（心怦怦跳）、にこにこ（微笑）、はらはら（提心吊胆）、むかむか（恶心／生气）、がんがん（头疼得厉害等）、ひりひり（火辣辣地疼）＋する；ぺこぺこ（肚子饿）、からから（干渴）、くたくた（疲惫不堪）＋だ。意思随语境变化。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.5.en: The manual lists the words of physical feeling: むずむず (Itchy sobs) どきどき (heart beats) にこにこ (Smiling) はらはら (EXHALES) むかむか (disgusting/grunting) がんがん (headache waiting) ひりひり (spiring) + する ； ぺこぺこ (I'm hungry.) からから (Dry) くたくた ♪ Tired ♪ だ . Meaning changes in context.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.6.zh: 先表达说话人的感受，再说明引起这种感受的事情。常见「驚いたことに」「面白いことに」「残念なことに」。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.4.grammar.6.en: Express the speaker's feeling first, then explain what caused it. Common forms include 驚いたことに、面白いことに、残念なことに.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.0.zh: 书面语，表示动作或作用向某一方向逐渐变化。常与変化する、変わる、増加する、増える、減少する、減る、なる等搭配。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.0.en: Written expression for gradual change in a direction. Often used with 変化する、変わる、増加する、増える、減少する、減る、なる.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.1.zh: 以某个地点、事物或人群为中心或主要对象。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.1.en: A particular location, thing or group of persons is central or the main target.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.2.zh: 本课表示地点。「に」标示存在地点，「で」标示动作发生地点。不要与表示时间的「たところ」混淆。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.2.en: This course shows the location. " に " indicates where it exists, and " で " indicates where the action is taking place. Do not confuse with "たところ " which represents the time.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.3.zh: 意志动词表示能够由本人决定做不做的行为。非意志动词表示存在、自然现象、能力或自然感知等，不能只凭本人意志控制；可能形式如「行ける」属于后者。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.3.en: Will verb indicates that it is possible to do the act in its own right. Non-consensual verb means existence, natural phenomena, ability or perception of nature, etc., cannot be controlled solely by its own will; the Potential form form, like " 行ける " , belongs to the latter.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.4.zh: 表示典型性，给人“很像……、很有……特点”的感觉。本课不是表示传闻或推测的「らしい」。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.4.en: This course is not about anecdotal or speculative "らしい."

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.5.zh: 表示从外表观察到的神情或样子，用法相当于表示样态的「そう」。「～げ」整体按な形容词使用。本课提示不用于长辈或上级。例：楽しげ、悲しげ、寂しげ、恥ずかしげ、得意げ。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.5.grammar.5.en: Describes an outward appearance or expression, similar to appearance-based そう. ～げ behaves as a na-adjective. This lesson advises against using it for elders or superiors. Examples: 楽しげ、悲しげ、寂しげ、恥ずかしげ、得意げ。

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.0.zh: 教材对照：本ではない→本じゃない；食べてしまった→食べちゃった；飲んでしまった→飲んじゃった；食べなければ→食べなきゃ；食べています→食べてます；食べている→食べてる；食べておく→食べとく；食べておいて→食べといて；食べるのだ→食べるんだ。转折「しかし・だが・が」在口语中常用「だけど・けど・でも」，「ですから」对应「だから」。用于日常口语，注意场合与语气。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.0.en: Textbook comparisons: 本ではない→本じゃない; 食べてしまった→食べちゃった; 飲んでしまった→飲んじゃった; 食べなければ→食べなきゃ; 食べています→食べてます; 食べている→食べてる; 食べておく→食べとく; 食べておいて→食べといて; 食べるのだ→食べるんだ. In conversation, しかし・だが・が often become だけど・けど・でも, and ですから becomes だから. Consider the situation and tone when using these everyday forms.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.1.zh: 后面接判断或评价，用来说明从某人的立场看某事的意义、难易或重要性等。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.1.en: It is then judged or evaluated to indicate the meaning, difficulty or importance of something from a person ' s position.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.2.zh: 表示感情或欲望难以抑制，无法不做某件事。「は」可以省略。不是单纯的义务或规定。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.2.en: The expression of feelings or desires is hard to contain and cannot do anything. " は " can be omitted. It is not simply an obligation or a regulation.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.3.zh: 根据客观信息进行判断或转述消息，带有与所说事情保持一定距离的感觉。与第5课表示典型特征的「Nらしい」区分。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.3.en: Distinguish ～らしい based on evidence or reports from the noun + らしい pattern in Lesson 5, which describes typical qualities.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.4.zh: 提出假定条件，在此基础上思考结果、选择或应采取的行动。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.4.en: The assumption is made, on the basis of which the results, choices or actions to be taken are considered.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.5.zh: 本课「（という）ことになる」表示由条件或事实推论出的结果。「ことになっている」表示由规则或他人决定的事；「ことにしている」表示自己决定并持续实行的个人习惯。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.5.en: Here （という）ことになる introduces a result inferred from facts or conditions. ことになっている describes a rule or decision made by others; ことにしている describes a personal decision maintained as a habit.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.6.zh: 教材图表题目为「朝何も食べない人の割合」：20多岁男性18.3％，60多岁男性1.6％。资料依据厚生劳动省《平成29年（2017年）国民健康・栄養調査結果の概要》。这是教材引用的历史数据，用于练习图表表达。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.6.grammar.6.en: The textbook chart is titled 朝何も食べない人の割合: 18.3% of men in their twenties and 1.6% of men in their sixties. The textbook cites the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's 平成29年（2017年）国民健康・栄養調査結果の概要. These are historical textbook figures used to practice describing charts.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.0.zh: 表示大量同类事物存在，通常是不理想的状态，如泥、伤、错误等。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.0.en: It means that a great deal of the same kind exists, usually in an undesirable state, such as mud, injury, error, etc.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.1.zh: 「ないと」提出否定条件，「ないからだ」说明理由。常用来解释为什么必须进行某种行为；后半句也可用「命の保証がない」等否定表达。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.1.en: ないと introduces a negative condition; ないからだ explains the reason. The pattern often explains why an action is necessary. The latter clause may use another negative expression such as 命の保証がない.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.2.zh: 表示每次发生某事时，总会伴随另一个结果。本课强调不用于日常生活中理所当然的事情，例如“每次早上起床就洗脸”。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.2.en: This lesson emphasizes things that are not taken for granted in everyday life, such as “show your face every morning when you wake up.”

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.3.zh: 在已有的事物或情况上再增加另一项，多用于书面语。教材动词接续列有辞书形、ない形和た形。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.3.en: に加え（て） adds another fact to an existing situation, often in written language. The textbook lists dictionary, ない and た forms for verbs; check the noun and adjective patterns separately.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.4.zh: 这里的「は」提示最低所需的数量或程度，不是单纯提示话题。教材中的饮食和睡眠例句用于理解句型。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.4.en: The minimum number or degree of " は" here is not simply the subject. The diet and sleep example in the material is used to understand the sentence.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.5.zh: 转述他人要求做某事或不要做某事。本课不是表示目的的「ように」。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.5.en: Repeals a request to do something or not to do something. This course is not "ように " for the purpose.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.6.zh: 本课表示显现、出现，不是单纯向说话人方向移动。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.6.en: This course shows, shows up and does not simply move in the direction of those who speak.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.7.zh: 接续词：だから（所以）、すると（于是）、したがって（因此）、そのため（为此／因此）、しかし（但是）、だが（但是）。副词：まず（首先）、再び（再次）、ようやく（终于）、たっぷり（充分地）、大量に（大量地）、さらに（更加／进一步）、はっきり（清楚地）。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.7.grammar.7.en: Structure word: だから (So) すると (thus) したがって (as a result), そのため (for this/as a result), しかし (But), だが (but) Adverbs: まず (first of all), 再び (Again), ようやく # At last # たっぷり (fullness), 大量に (many of them), さらに (more/further), はっきり (clears throat)

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.0.zh: 强调数量、程度或性质有限，相当于“仅此而已”。与表示“过于……”的「すぎる」不同。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.0.en: The emphasis is limited in number, degree or nature, which amounts to " nothing more than this " , unlike "すぎる" for "excessive".

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.1.zh: 假设唯一的必要条件，强调满足这个条件即可。例：天気さえよければ、体さえ丈夫なら。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.1.en: Presents a single necessary condition and emphasizes that meeting it is sufficient. Examples: 天気さえよければ、体さえ丈夫なら.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.2.zh: 本课「さえ」与条件表达搭配；「しか」必须与否定形式呼应；「こそ」突出强调对象。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.2.en: This lesson "さえ" matches conditional expressions; "しか" must respond to negative forms; and "こそ" highlights objects.

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.3.zh: 否定简单、绝对的判断，表示并不是任何时候都必然如此，类似「わけではない／わけでもない」。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.3.en: Rejecting simple, absolute judgements means that this is not always necessary, like "わけではない/ わけでもない " .

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.4.zh: 表示由于某种原因可能产生不好的结果。不是“不能”的意思；注意与「かねる」区分。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.4.en: This means that a bad result may occur for some reason. It is not meant to be "can't"; attention is distinguished from "かねる".

chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.5.zh: 承认前项事实，但后项情况与通常预期不同，相当于「けれども」，多用于书面表达。
chukyu-o-manabo-chukyu-zenki.8.grammar.5.en: Recognition of the previous fact, but the latter situation is different from normal expectations and amounts to " けれども " , which is mostly used for written expression.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.1.t.zh: 是呀。不过周一有考试，周末得学习啊。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.1.t.en: Yeah. But there's an exam Monday, so I have to study over the weekend.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.2.t.zh: 嗯……那个，不好意思，能把笔记借我一下吗？我缺了好多课，落下了不少内容。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.2.t.en: Um... so, hey, sorry to ask, but can you lend me your notes? I've missed a lot of classes, so I'm pretty behind.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.3.t.zh: 哎呀，这么赶可不行。我自己也要用。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.3.t.en: Aw, that's cutting it way too close, no can do. I need them too.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.4.t.zh: 也是……那，明天或周日，能一起学习吗？到时候让我看看你的笔记怎么样？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.4.t.en: Yeah... Then, can you study with me tomorrow or Sunday? How about you let me see your notes then?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.6.t.en: So which is better? Tomorrow? Sunday?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.7.t.zh: 嗯——都行，不过要不明天就搞定？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.7.t.en: Hmm, either's fine, but why not just do it tomorrow?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.8.t.zh: 嗯，那就明天吧。真是帮大忙了。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.0.line.8.t.en: OK, let's do tomorrow then. You're a lifesaver.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.1.line.2.t.zh: 哥，圣诞节爸爸给你买的那游戏，你还在玩吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.1.line.2.t.en: Bro, that game Dad bought you for Christmas—are you still playing it?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.1.line.3.t.en: Nah, I haven't played it lately.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.1.line.4.t.zh: 朋友说想让我借给他，我能借到吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.1.line.4.t.en: A friend asked me to lend it to them, so I was wondering if I could borrow it.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.1.line.5.t.zh: 啊，行是行。不过我朋友也说要借，所以可能没法马上给你。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.1.line.5.t.en: Ah, sure. But my friend also wants to borrow it, so probably not right away.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.1.line.7.t.zh: 啊，这个嘛——可能要过一阵子，下个月左右吧。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.1.line.7.t.en: Ah, let's see... probably a while off, like next month maybe.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.1.line.8.t.zh: 啊，这样啊。那到时候再告诉我一声好吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.1.line.8.t.en: Oh, I see. Then can you let me know when the time comes?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.0.t.zh: 那个，山田小姐，我有件事想拜托你。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.0.t.en: Um, Yamada-san, I have a favor to ask.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.2.t.zh: 如果不行也没关系，山田小姐，你有一个黑色的手提包吧？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.2.t.en: It's fine if you can't, but Yamada-san, you have a black handbag, right?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.4.t.zh: 就是那个，拎手是珍珠做的包。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.4.t.en: You know, the one with the pearl handle.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.6.t.zh: 那个，我有朋友的婚礼要参加，可是我没有适合那种场合背的包。所以，如果方便的话，下周末能借我一下吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.6.t.en: See, I have a friend's wedding to go to, and I don't have a bag I can take to that kind of place. So, if it's OK, could you lend it to me next weekend?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.8.t.zh: 对。一直工作很忙，没时间去买。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.8.t.en: Yes. I've been so busy with work I haven't had time to go buy one.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.10..zh: 那个，不过不行也没关系。我今天或明天早点把工作做完，就去买。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.10..en: But it's fine if you can't. I'll finish work early today or tomorrow and go buy one.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.11..zh: 可是你也没什么时间吧。现在正是最忙的时候。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.11..en: But you hardly have time, right? It's your busiest time now.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.13..zh: 那个包你要是觉得行就拿去用吧。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.13..en: If that one's OK with you, please go ahead and take it.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.14..zh: 真的可以吗？太高兴了。太好了——周一我就还你。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.14..en: Really? I'm so happy. Great! I'll return it on Monday.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.15..en: Then I'll bring it to the office tomorrow.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.2.line.16..en: Thank you. I'm counting on you.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.2.t.zh: 那个，吉本同学，你选了叫‘经营概论’的课吧？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.2.t.en: Um, Yoshimoto-san, you took the course called 'Introduction to Management,' right?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.4.t.zh: 对吧，因为是一年级的必修课。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.4.t.en: Right, because it's a required course for first-years.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.6.t.zh: 那个，我想拜托你，那门课的课本能借我吗？是叫《经营学基础》之类的名字的课本。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.6.t.en: Um, I was wondering, could you lend me the textbook for that course? It's called something like 'Basics of Management Studies.'

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.8.t.zh: 哇，帮大忙了。那本书很贵吧。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.8.t.en: Wow, that's a relief. That book is expensive, isn't it?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.9.t.zh: 我想我也用不到了，干脆送你吧？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.9.t.en: I don't think I'll use it either, so why don't I just give it to you?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.10..zh: 不，那怎么行。太不好意思了。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.10..en: No, that's OK. I'd feel bad.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.11..zh: 这样啊。那我什么时候带给你好？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.11..en: I see. So when should I bring it?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.12..zh: 不好意思，我只有周二第二节有课，能在那之前借到就太感谢了。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.12..en: I'm sorry, but I only have class on Tuesday 2nd period, so I'd be grateful if I could borrow it before then.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.13..zh: 那我周一带到学校来吧。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.13..en: Then I'll bring it to school on Monday.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.15..zh: 那中午在学校食堂碰面？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.15..en: So shall we meet at the school cafeteria for lunch?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.16..zh: 好。那12点左右，在食堂前面见面吧。可以吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.16..en: Yes. So around 12, shall we meet in front of the cafeteria? Is that OK?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.3.line.18..en: Sorry for the trouble. Thanks for your help.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.4.line.0.t.zh: 我打算周六去钓鱼，可我没有保鲜箱。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.4.line.0.t.en: I'm planning to go fishing Saturday, but I don't have a cooler box.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.4.line.2.t.zh: 所以，如果你没用的话，能借我吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.4.line.2.t.en: So, if you're not using it, could you lend it to me?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.5.line.0.t.zh: 姐姐，姐姐你的黑色包，周日能借我吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.5.line.0.t.en: Sis, can I borrow your black bag on Sunday?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.5.line.1.t.zh: 周日？抱歉，不行。你看，我有婚礼要参加。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.5.line.1.t.en: Sunday? Sorry, can't. See, I have a wedding to go to.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.5.line.2.t.zh: 啊，对哦。我忘了。……那米色的能借吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.5.line.2.t.en: Oh, right, I forgot. ...Then can I borrow the beige one?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.6.line.0.t.zh: 我说，自行车能借我吗？我的爆胎了。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.6.line.0.t.en: Hey, can I borrow your bike? Mine got a flat.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.6.line.1.t.zh: 啊，不好意思。我正准备现在出门买东西。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.6.line.1.t.en: Ah, sorry. I was just about to go shopping now.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.6.line.2.t.zh: 这样啊，知道了。那等你回来能借我吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.6.line.2.t.en: I see, got it. Then can I borrow it when you get back?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.6.line.3.t.zh: 啊，行。我大概一小时就回来。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.6.line.3.t.en: Sure. I'll be back in about an hour.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.7.line.0.t.zh: 大森先生，研讨室的桌子能借一下吗？我想用一下。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.7.line.0.t.en: Omori-san, may I use the table in the seminar room? I need to use it for a bit.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.7.line.1.t.zh: 啊，不好意思。我现在就要开会。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.7.line.1.t.en: Ah, sorry. I have a meeting starting now.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.7.line.2.t.en: Oh, I see. Then it's fine.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.8.line.0.t.zh: 那个，不好意思，这台复印机能让我用一下吗？我们部门的现在坏了。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.8.line.0.t.en: Excuse me, could you let me use this copier? The one in our department is broken right now.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.8.line.1.t.zh: 抱歉。我马上要开会，现在正用着。30分钟以后可以吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.8.line.1.t.en: I'm sorry. I have a meeting soon and I'm using it now. Would 30 minutes later work?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.8.line.2.t.zh: 可以，当然。那我待会儿再来。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.8.line.2.t.en: Yes, of course. Then I'll come back later.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.9.line.0.t.zh: 不好意思，能借我点钱吗？我没带现金。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.9.line.0.t.en: Sorry, can you lend me some money? I don't have any cash on me.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.9.line.1.t.en: Oh, sure. Is about 2000 yen OK?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.10.line.0..zh: 那个，你有做演示用的打印机吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.10.line.0..en: Um, do you have a printer you use for presentations?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.10.line.2..zh: 我明天要做演示，能借我吗？
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.10.line.2..en: I have a presentation tomorrow—could you lend it to me?

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.10.line.4..en: That's a big help. Thank you.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.11.line.0..zh: 那个，关于共用的笔记本电脑……

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.11.line.2..zh: 我后天出差要带去用，能让我用一下吗？归还的话要等到周四。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.11.line.2..en: Could you let me use it for a business trip the day after tomorrow? I'd return it on Thursday.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.11.line.3..zh: 可以呀。如果没人用的话就没问题。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.11.line.3..en: Yes, sure. As long as no one else is using it, it's fine.

nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.12.line.0..zh: 我说，山田。我有样东西想借。
nihongo-namachukei.1.dialogue.12.line.0..en: Hey, Yamada. There's something I want to borrow.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.0.t.zh: 啊，我们周日说好要带孩子们去游乐园的吧。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.0.t.en: Oh, we agreed to take the kids to the amusement park on Sunday, right?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.2.t.zh: 啊，不好意思，能改到下周吗？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.2.t.en: Ah, sorry, but can we do it next week instead?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.4.t.zh: 我有件非得周末完成不可的工作。真的，对孩子们也很过意不去。你看，周六我们还要去看奶奶（探病）吧。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.4.t.en: There's work I absolutely have to get done on the weekend. I really feel bad for the kids too. See, we're supposed to visit Grandma on Saturday, right?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.5.t.zh: 你就不能想办法把周日空出来吗？孩子们也很期待呢。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.5.t.en: Can't you somehow manage to keep Sunday free? The kids are looking forward to it.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.6.t.zh: 嗯——可是工作堆着，恐怕很难。真的抱歉。下周周末我一定空出来。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.6.t.en: Hmm, but work has piled up, so it's tough. Really, sorry. I'll definitely keep next weekend free, OK?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.7.t.zh: 下周，说定了哦。你要自己好好跟孩子们解释。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.0.line.7.t.en: Next week, for sure. And you explain it properly to the kids yourself.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.3.t.zh: 那个，关于今晚坂本室长的欢送会……
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.3.t.en: Um, about Director Sakamoto's farewell party tonight...

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.5.t.zh: 孩子有点发烧，在妻子回来之前我出不了门。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.5.t.en: My child has a bit of a fever, so I can't go out until my wife gets home.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.7.t.zh: 嗯，不过我想跟坂本先生打个招呼，所以可能会晚到一点，但我打算过去。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.7.t.en: Yes, but I want to say goodbye to Sakamoto-san, so I might be a bit late, but I plan to come.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.9.t.zh: 所以，能不能不等我，先开始？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.9.t.en: So, could you start without waiting for me?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.13..zh: 那不好意思，能帮我把这个告诉大家吗？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.13..en: Then could you please pass that along to everyone?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.15..zh: 谢谢你。不好意思，就拜托你了。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.1.line.15..en: Thank you. Sorry for the trouble, but I'm counting on you.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.3.t.zh: 那个，抱歉。关于今天的约定，我头有点疼，吃了药也不见好。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.3.t.en: Um, sorry. About our plan today—my head hurts for some reason, and even medicine isn't helping.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.5.t.zh: 嗯，那个，不好意思，去海边能不能改到明天，不去今天？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.5.t.en: Yeah, well, sorry, but can we go to the beach tomorrow instead of today?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.6.t.zh: 这样啊。可以呀。头疼的话也玩不痛快嘛。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.6.t.en: I see. Sure. If your head hurts, you can't enjoy it anyway.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.8.t.zh: 没事没事。别在意。比起那个，你还是好好休息比较好。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.8.t.en: It's fine, it's fine. Don't worry about it. More importantly, you should rest well.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.10..zh: 到了晚上要是还不舒服，明天可能也得取消比较好哦。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.10..en: If you still feel bad even by tonight, maybe we should call off tomorrow too.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.11..zh: 也是。那今晚再电话联系吧。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.11..en: Yeah. Then I'll call you again tonight.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.12..zh: 嗯。那今天你就好好休息吧。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.2.line.12..en: Yeah. So take it easy today.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.3.line.3.t.zh: 我是预约了明天周六6点的米田。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.3.line.3.t.en: I'm Yoneida, who made a reservation for tomorrow Saturday at 6.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.3.line.5.t.zh: 突然打扰很抱歉，能改到7点吗？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.3.line.5.t.en: I'm sorry for the sudden change, but is it possible to change it to 7?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.3.line.6.t.zh: 请稍等。我现在确认一下。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.3.line.6.t.en: Just a moment, please. I'll check now.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.3.line.8.t.zh: 让您久等了。那个，因为是周六有点挤，不过7点半的话可以。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.3.line.8.t.en: Thank you for waiting. Um, since it's Saturday it's a bit crowded, but 7:30 would be fine.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.4.line.2.t.zh: 很抱歉，我突然有急事。所以我想会晚到30分钟左右，能帮我跟大家说一下吗？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.4.line.2.t.en: I'm sorry, but something urgent came up. So I think I'll be about 30 minutes late—could you let everyone know?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.5.line.0.t.en: Um, about the movie on Saturday...

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.5.line.2.t.zh: 因为工作关系，周六我得去公司。能不能改到下周？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.5.line.2.t.en: Due to work, I have to go to the office on Saturday. Can we do it next week instead?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.5.line.4.t.en: Sorry. I'll treat you next time, OK?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.6.line.2.t.zh: 抱歉。周日我得出差去大阪。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.6.line.2.t.en: Sorry. I got assigned a business trip to Osaka on Sunday.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.6.line.3.t.zh: 这样啊。是工作的话也没办法。行呀行呀。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.6.line.3.t.en: I see. If it's work, can't be helped. It's fine, it's fine.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.7.line.0.t.zh: 老师，不好意思。今天关于小组项目，课后我本该去您研究室的……
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.7.line.0.t.en: Professor, sorry. Today, about the group project, I was supposed to visit your office after class...

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.7.line.2.t.zh: 那个，我从昨天起一直发烧不退。很抱歉，能不能改到别的日子？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.7.line.2.t.en: Um, since yesterday I've had a fever that won't go down. I'm very sorry, but would it be possible to reschedule to another day?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.7.line.3.t.zh: 可以呀，没问题。稍等一下，我看一下日程。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.7.line.3.t.en: Yes, that's fine. No problem. Just a moment—let me check my schedule.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.8.line.0.t.zh: 关于今天的碰头会，我突然有急事。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.8.line.0.t.en: About today's meeting—something urgent came up.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.8.line.2.t.zh: 所以不好意思，能不能把开始时间推迟30分钟？可以吗？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.8.line.2.t.en: So, I'm sorry, but could you delay the start time by 30 minutes? Is that OK?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.9.line.0.t.en: Hey, about the meal on Saturday...

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.9.line.2.t.zh: 我有点事，得去公司了。所以不好意思，能改到下周吗？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.9.line.2.t.en: Something came up and I have to go to the office. So, sorry, but can we do it next week?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.9.line.3.t.zh: 下周啊——等一下，我看下日程。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.9.line.3.t.en: Next week? Hang on, let me check my schedule.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.10.line.2..zh: 那个，关于交换留学，我本该今天去您那儿拜访的……
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.10.line.2..en: Um, about the exchange program—I believe I was supposed to come see you today...

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.10.line.4..zh: 因为签证的事我得去大使馆，非常抱歉，能不能改到别的日子？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.10.line.4..en: But I have to go to the embassy for my visa, and I'm terribly sorry—could we do it another day instead?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.10.line.5..zh: 别的时间的话，是何时呢？
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.10.line.5..en: Another day, you say—when did you have in mind?

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.11.line.0..en: Hello, this is Hair Salon Tink.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.11.line.1..zh: 那个，我是预约了今天5点的武田。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.11.line.1..en: Um, I'm Takeda, who made a reservation for 5 today.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.11.line.2..en: Oh, thank you for your continued patronage.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.11.line.3..zh: 那个，能改到4点吗？很突然，不好意思。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.11.line.3..en: Um, could you make it 4 instead? Sorry for the sudden change.

nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.11.line.4..zh: 今天的4点对吧。好的，知道了。我们恭候您。
nihongo-namachukei.2.dialogue.11.line.4..en: 4 o'clock today, then. Yes, understood. We'll be expecting you.

nihongo-namachukei.3.dialogue.0.line.3.t.en: Sure, go ahead. What would you like to drink?
